report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Render one council deliberation as markdown, with quorum honesty, dissents first, evidence, cost/latency, turns, and provenance footer.

symbols.name: _bus_path
symbols.note: Determines canonical bus record path from transcript or verdict fields, else derives from council_id.

symbols.name: _turns_of
symbols.note: Normalizes transcript into a list of turns.

symbols.name: _chain_head
symbols.note: Extracts chain head digest from transcript or verdict fields, else last turn's entry_sha.

symbols.name: _quorum_counts
symbols.note: Returns (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors) from vendor lists or integers.

symbols.name: _evidence_paths
symbols.note: Flattens evidence items and paths into a list of path strings.

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Renders a council verdict as markdown with ordered sections and provenance footer.

claims.text: Where the canonical record lives. Explicit field wins; otherwise derived from the council id, which is how ``bus.py`` names the file.
claims.why: The function checks transcript fields then verdict fields, then falls back to council_id-derived path under DEFAULT_BUS_DIR.

claims.text: A transcript may be the turn list itself, or an object/dict carrying one.
claims.why: Handles None, Mapping, list/tuple, and objects with turns/records/entries fields.

claims.text: The chain head digest a reader verifies the bus against. Explicit field wins; otherwise the last turn's entry_sha, which IS the head by construction in an append-only chain.
claims.why: Checks transcript fields, then verdict fields, then last turn's entry_sha/sha/digest.

claims.text: (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors). Counts are derived from the vendor LISTS when present, because a list is checkable against the transcript and a bare integer is not.
claims.why: Uses vendor lists for answered/requested when integers are absent; missing computed from list difference.

claims.text: Paths named by the evidence, for the path-marker half of the floor.
claims.why: Collects path/file/label/name fields from evidence items plus the paths field.

claims.text: Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past.
claims.why: Outcome line appears before quorum; quorum warning appears before dissents and convergence.

claims.text: Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice.
claims.why: Dissents section is rendered before the convergence section, each with author and verbatim text.

claims.text: Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: Sections appear in that order: convergence, evidence, cost/latency, deliberation, then footer with bus_path and chain_head.

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: The function only builds strings and calls pure helpers; no imports or calls that perform I/O, network, or gating.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: The ADVISORY ONLY line is always appended, and a caution block is added when advisory is not True.

claims.text: A short council is a weaker signal and that must be impossible to miss -- it is a warning block, not a footnote.
claims.why: When answered < requested, a WARNING blockquote is emitted before other content.

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice.
claims.why: The Dissents section is placed before the convergence section.

claims.text: Rendering it after -- and therefore below -- the agreement makes the informative half read as a footnote to the uninformative half.
claims.why: The comment is a rationale; the code places dissents before convergence, so the claim about the alternative is not contradicted by this chunk.

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: The verbatim block is only appended when text is truthy.

claims.text: Convergence is an OBSERVATION about what these vendors said, not a decision and not a vote. Models with overlapping training data agreeing is not independent confirmation, and nothing here counts as a passed gate.
claims.why: The rendered text explicitly states this and no gate-related output is produced.

claims.text: bus.py records "refused" / "unavailable" / "budget_exhausted" / "anomaly" rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between "three vendors agreed" and "one was never asked".
claims.why: The claim about bus.py's recording behavior is outside this chunk; the rendering of statuses is present but the bus-side behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.
claims.why: The withheld list is rendered as named paths in a NOTE block, not as a count.

claims.text: This comment IS the rendering of the bus.
claims.why: The deliberation section renders turns from the transcript.

claims.text: Provenance footer: how to check this rendering against the record.
claims.why: The footer includes bus_path and chain_head, which are the verification anchors.

observations.what: _quorum_counts treats a non-int integer-like value (e.g., string "3") as absent and falls back to list length, potentially misreporting quorum when a numeric string is provided.
_quorum_counts sets requested = answered when requested is falsy, which may silently hide a missing quorum target.
render_markdown emits '**Quorum: {answered} of {requested} requested vendors answered** (full roster).' even when requested is 0 and answered is 0, which may be misleading if no roster was recorded.
The cost/latency table renders cost and latency as text without numeric formatting or unit checks; a malformed value like 'abc' would be shown as-is.

The verdict's 'advisory' field is only checked for truthiness; if it is a string like 'false', it is treated as non-True and the caution is shown, which is likely intended but not explicitly documented.

risks: _quorum_counts | medium | Non-int numeric strings for quorum counts are ignored, falling back to list lengths and potentially misreporting quorum | Provide a test with a string integer and verify the count derivation

_quorum_counts | medium | When requested is falsy, requested is set to answered, which can hide a missing quorum target | Inspect callers to see if requested=0 is a valid state that should be reported as missing
render_markdown | low | The full-roster message is emitted even when requested is 0, which may mislead readers about roster completeness | Add a check for requested == 0 and emit a different message
render_markdown | low | Cost/latency values are not validated; malformed data renders as-is, potentially confusing readers | Add a numeric validation or format check for cost and latency fields

render_markdown | low | The advisory field truthiness check may treat non-boolean truthy values (e.g., 'yes') as advisory, which is not documented | Clarify the expected type of advisory and handle non-boolean values explicitly
